description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy, with three distinct measures of accuracy—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—plotted against the x-axis labeled "Initial Confidence," which ranges from 0.86 to 1.00 in increments of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," spans from 0.0 to 1.0. The blue line, representing Final Accuracy, remains consistently high across the range of initial confidence, starting at approximately 0.95, peaking near 1.0 at an initial confidence of 0.97, and ending at about 0.98. The green line, representing Initial Accuracy, begins at approximately 0.65, increases to a peak of about 0.95 at an initial confidence of 0.97, and then declines to around 0.75 at an initial confidence of 1.0. The orange line, representing Δ Accuracy, starts at approximately 0.3, decreases to a low of about 0.05 at an initial confidence of 0.95, and then rises to about 0.25 at an initial confidence of 1.0. All three lines exhibit error bars, indicating variability in the data points.
